title: Refit a splash-shield panel with a push-in clip: hold its hole over the body's and push the clip home through both
instruction: Fasten the splash-shield panel to the body with the clip.
context: Splash shields, fender liners and underbody panels are held on by push-type retainers, and refitting them is routine in automotive service (BLS: automotive service technicians and mechanics held about 805,600 jobs in 2024). The panel lies loose on the body with its hole out of line, so one hand has to hold it with the two holes lined up while the other pushes the clip in, and then push its head home: a clip short of home, or through one hole only, doesn't hold the panel. A typical part: a nylon splash-shield retainer for an 8 mm hole with a 20 mm head (Lawson Products P53958).
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. Body (fixed): a grey steel flange 16 x 22 cm, 2 mm thick, held 4 cm above the table on four posts, centred at (30, 2), with an 11.4 mm square hole at (28, 9). Under the hole, the clip's catch: two steel rods 4 mm across and 12 mm long (along x), their tops 0.3 mm under the flange and 8.4 mm apart at rest; each slides straight out sideways (along y) up to 3 mm against a 300 N/m spring preloaded 0.5 mm (0.15 N at rest, 1.05 N at full travel). The clip's 9.6 mm collar spreads them 0.6 mm each as it passes, and they close under it round the 7.6 mm stem, which holds the clip. Splash-shield panel (loose): black polypropylene, 8 x 20 cm, 2.5 mm thick, 50 g, flat on the flange, with an 11.4 mm square hole 7 cm left of its middle and a 15 mm lip standing up along its right-hand edge; it starts with its middle at (29, 1.2), its hole 10 mm farther out and 8 mm to the right of the body's. Push-in clip (loose): black nylon, 5 g, octagonal throughout (sizes across the flats), 19 mm long in all: a head 20 mm across and 3 mm thick; under it a 7.6 mm stem, 11 mm long; then a 9.6 mm collar, 3 mm thick (11 to 14 mm below the head's underside); then a 6 mm tip, 2 mm long. Going in, the collar's bottom edge meets the rods' round faces 0.6 mm below their tops, with the head's underside 8.6 mm above the panel, and is past the rods (its top below their undersides) once the head is within 2.2 mm of the panel; seated flush, the collar's top is 2.2 mm below the rods' undersides and the rods close round the stem above it. The clip stands head up in the 11.4 mm square hole of a grey plastic tray block (4 cm square, 2 cm tall) at (22, 20). Every loose object has friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic. Both grippers start open at the ready pose.
scoring: At the end. Lined up: the panel flat on the flange (within 3 degrees, its underside within 1 mm of the flange) with its hole within 1.5 mm of the body's. Home: the clip upright (within 5 degrees) with its axis within 1.5 mm of the hole's, its collar's top below the catch rods' undersides (the rods closed over it), and its head's underside within 1 mm of the panel. 1.0: lined up and the clip home, everything still, held for 1 s, which ends the trial (if time runs out before that has held, it scores 0.9). 0.5: lined up with the clip through and held but its head more than 1 mm proud. 0.25: lined up with no clip through it. 0 otherwise, including the panel out of line, tilted or off the flange.
reset_notes: Lay the panel back on its marks on the flange, out of line, and stand the clip head up in its tray; take a clip out of the catch by spreading its jaws.
fidelity: The flange is fixed. Real retainer barbs are on the clip and flex; here the clip is rigid and the barbs are two sprung jaws in the hole that the clip's collar pushes apart and then sits under. The holes are 11.4 mm square, not 8 mm round, so the rigid collar can pass both with up to 1.5 mm of misalignment. The clip is an octagonal prism made of boxes; it weighs 5 g (a real one about 2 g).
